properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 2:53PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco and
Monterey Bays.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 1:04PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and elevated surf are expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be expected
near times of high tide.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There
is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.1
to 7.3 feet on Tuesday morning.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Wasatch Mountains South of I-80
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 12 at 1:51PM MDT until October 14 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected, particularly for elevations above 8,500ft.
Total snow accumulations up to 4 to 6 inches in upper Little and
Big Cottonwood, with higher amounts expected for elevations above
9,000ft.

* WHERE...Wasatch Mountains South of I-80.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM MDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Early season snowfall on roadways may pose a
significant risk to under-prepared travelers. While minor snow
accumulations are expected for upper Little and Big Cottonwood
Canyon, Guardsman Pass will likely see higher snowfall potential.
If traveling along this route, be prepared for winter driving
conditions.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For winter road conditions
from the Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

For graphical depictions of the snowfall forecast, including Official
NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.
